title: Added AI voiceovers to my game
author: MoneySquirrel1910
selftext:
I'm developing a visual novel game where you play as a king making decisions with your councillors. The goal is to get the kingdom to survive until the end.

I decided to add AI voiceovers to the dialogue. Hiring professional voice actors for a dialogue-heavy game like this would cost thousands of dollars and require lots of time and equipment. Instead I used DialogueCraft, paid nothing and within minutes got dozens of high-quality voicelines.

Do you have any feedback?

comments.author: Useful_Armadillo317
comments.body: would love to do that same, but with these being online only/paid cant confirm the site would even be active by the time the game is nearly finished, how is local text to voice?

replies.author: MoneySquirrel1910
replies.body:
Sorry I don't understand your question.

I download the voice lines directly as mp3 files, and then import them into the engine. The site doesn't need to be active for my downloaded files to work.

replies.author: Useful_Armadillo317
replies.body: okay, i mean your doing this through a website correct? its not done locally, so if the website is removed or goes out of business no more voice lines

comments.author: beneficialdiet18
comments.body: Love the art style. What did you use for assets?

replies.author: MoneySquirrel1910
replies.body:
Thank you! 

The characters are part of a asset pack from [itch.io](http://itch.io), they are not AI. The voicelines are generated through [dialoguecraft.net](http://dialoguecraft.net)

replies.author: BluddyCurry
replies.body: Very cool. How many credits did it take to do the game so far?

comments.author: Working_Benefit_3289
comments.body:
Male voices sound awesome (for a non-native speaker at least). I would probably never guess they are AI. Maybe a single fragment from Falk was suspicious. 
But the female voice sounds too similar to the AIs popular on the internet. Could you improve/tweak it a bit?

Anyway, nice job!

replies.author: MoneySquirrel1910
replies.body:
Thank you so much and I appreciate the feedback!

You're right that the female voice is a bit generic, she uses a very popular AI voice. I will switch to a voice that sounds less "AI".

comments.author: Epyx911
comments.body: Are you using Elevenlabs V3? I am myself for some characters in my narration and it has REALLY impressed me...particularly the voice designer.

replies.author: MoneySquirrel1910
replies.body:
Yes I am using DialogueCraft.net which uses the ElevenLabs V3 api but is more optimized for game development.

I really would like to use the voice designer tool, but in my experience I feel like the quality is only good in the audio preview and when you actually use the voice the quality drops. That's why so far I have stuck to only using the professional voice clones.

replies.author: jeffersonianMI
replies.body: I tested Eleven Labs a year or two ago. Very impressed but I never pressed it on emotions. Could  [DialogueCraft.net](http://DialogueCraft.net) do stress, distress, or commanding tones convincingly? Or would it need the emotion in the sample do you think?

comments.author: yes4me2
comments.body: What is DialogueCraft? I have not heard of it.

replies.author: MoneySquirrel1910
replies.body: It's a web application that uses ElevenLabs V3 api for text-to-speech. For game development with heavy dialogue, it is far better and more efficient than just using ElevenLabs directly.

comments.author: samuelazers
comments.body: Amazing how it amazing to replicate the fiverr voice with the over-acting, poltus' bad accent and low volume, really makes it sound like an indie-game, not AI.

comments.author: Erik_malkavia
comments.body: This would be a great set of voices for a Motion Comic.  Great job
